title: Nonzero locally principal ideals on integral schemes are invertible
statement: Let X be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] and J a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. If J is locally principal and J ≠ 0, then J is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal].

proof.text: Choose a principal affine neighborhood U of a point with generator b. If b were zero, J vanishes on U. Every nonempty affine W meets U by irreducibility. Restrict a section of J on W to a basic affine neighborhood of a point in the intersection; it becomes zero. Injectivity of germs for the integral structure sheaf makes the original section zero. Empty affine opens have the zero ring, so J vanishes on them too. This contradicts J ≠ 0. Thus b is nonzero in the domain of sections on U and is a nonzerodivisor.
